items.title: Austin Ekeler rushed seven times for 41 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding three yards on two receptions.
items.text: The box score does little to jump off the page but it is notable that Ekeler played over Rachaad White as the primary change of pace option behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Whether that was due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week remains to be seen. Either way, the only fantasy-viable back currently on the roster appears to be Croskey-Merritt, leaving both Ekeler and White of little value moving forward. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 23 yards on two receptions.
items.text: Croskey-Merritt immediately returned from injured reserve to handily lead the team in snaps and opportunities, despite veteran Austin Ekeler playing the team’s first series. More interesting was the fact that Rachaad White hardly had a role, with Ekeler serving as the primary change of pace option, something that could be due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week. Either way, Croskey-Merritt appears to have a stranglehold on lead duties moving forward, a role that keeps him as a viable RB2 in the immediate future. That holds true for a Week 12 meeting with the Cardinals.

items.title: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-35 passes for 289 yards in the Commanders’ 22-20, Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 55 yards on six carries.
items.text: Daniels and the Commanders were unable to get anything going offensively while playing through driving rain in the first half, going three-and-out on three of their first four possessions before their lone touchdown drive of the game on their final possessions before the break. Things would change in the second half as Daniels led five consecutive scoring drives, all of which ended in field goals, proving enough to eek out a victory that could have saved the team’s season. items.title: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-9 targets for 31 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
items.text: The two teams played to a scoreless first frame through driving rain in Maryland, with Chase appearing to come alive on the teams first possession of the second quarter. He would ultimately be locked up by sticky coverage heavily influenced by Washington’s ability to generate consistent pressure, narrowly missing a downfield shot in the second half in triple coverage that could have propelled his fantasy day toward a usable week. items.title: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-3 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
items.text: Higgins got in the box score with a 31-yard touchdown reception late in the second quarter after the two teams played to a scoreless first frame in driving rain. The Bengals did not alter their typical pass-heavy ways despite the rain throughout the first half, with Higgins seeing modest volume while primarily matched up against Rasul Douglas on the perimeter. items.title: Mike Gesicki caught 5-of-6 targets for 77 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
items.text: Gesicki saw increased usage against an aggressive Commanders team that brought consistent pressure into the backfield, with the highlight of his game coming on a 32-yard reception over the middle of the field on the team’s final possession, ultimately ended in a field goal to take the lead with just over two minutes remaining. The Commanders would drive the field and kick the game-winning field goal on the subsequent possession to send the Bengals to 7-3. items.title: Samaje Perine rushed six times for 26 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 71 yards on four receptions.
items.text: The highlight of the game for Perine came on a 44-yard catch-and-run reception where he chipped into a leak route in the flat, springing free from linebacker coverage to give quarterback Joe Burrow an outlet in the face of pressure. He would outrun the secondary and pick up a key block from fellow running back Chase Brown as he sprung free down the sideline for the longest reception in the game. Perine’s 10 opportunities still ranked below the 14 of Brown but the former handily outproduced the presumed starter on his way to a usable fantasy outing. items.title: Chase Brown rushed six times for six yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders, adding 30 yards on five receptions.
items.text: Brown saw minimal usage in the first half as the two teams played through driving rain, likely equal parts known tendencies as it was matchup-based. The bigger story here was the involvement of Samaje Perine, who did more than his standard change of pace role implied on his way to 97 total yards. There was no mention of injury or anything that would suggest Brown’s role was limited by necessity, likely best viewed as a small blip on the fantasy radar. Brown’s next opportunity to return a usable fantasy week comes in Week 12 against the Saints, where he will remain a fantasy RB2. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Roschon Johnson (ankle) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.text: Johnson departed the team’s Week 11 win over the Saints with an ankle injury and did not return, making his absence Monday notable on the short week. Expect D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai to dominate snaps and opportunities out of the backfield for the Bears in one of the biggest games of the season, with the winner left standing alone atop the competitive NFC North. - Mark Garcia
